A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CogFlow study. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and complete Appendices A–D are available and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original CogFlow benchmark evaluations, component ablations, efficiency measurements and case studies in Section 4 and Appendix D.

after.justification: v3 retains the original benchmark results, ablations, efficiency measurements and case studies reported in v1.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Appendix C retain the same three-stage framework, synergistic visual rewards, knowledge internalization reward, Softmax-DPO training and visual-gated policy optimization. Algorithm 1 changes only title capitalization.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same MATHCOG training subsets and evaluate FlowVerse, MathVerse, MathVista, WeMath, LogicVista and DynaMath. No additional dataset, task, domain or test scenario is introduced.

E2.justification: Benchmark comparator sets, RL optimizer comparisons in Table 13 and encoder alternatives in Table 17 are unchanged. Vanilla DPO was already evaluated in Figure 6 of v1; v3 adds its citation without adding a comparator.

E3.justification: The reported splits, preprocessing, metrics, training budgets, model configurations and testing procedures remain unchanged. Appendix D retains the same controlled inference comparisons and training-time and inference-time gate sampling experiments.

E4.justification: Section 4.3 and Appendix D contain the same component, error-type, optimizer, gate, model-scale, reward-mixing and encoder analyses. The perception-error compensation and other case studies were already present in v1.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is unchanged, including the existing distribution plots. v3 adds no repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, significance tests or uncertainty-estimation procedures.

E6.justification: Numerical results and qualitative findings are retained throughout the main text and appendices. For example, Table 1 reports CogFlow's FlowVerse CoT-E/accuracy as 66.0/56.2 in both versions, and Table 3 retains 76.8% MathVista accuracy.

T1.justification: Equations 1–14, Algorithm 1, reward definitions, optimization objectives and mathematical reasoning are unchanged. No formal assumption, derivation, proof or theoretical result is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution statements and conclusion retain the same claims about CogFlow, MATHCOG, mitigating reasoning drift and improving visual mathematical reasoning. The added citations do not alter these claims.

C2.justification: The explanations of complementary rewards, cognitive internalization and error compensation remain unchanged. Appendix A.4 retains the computational-resource limitation and proposed extension to general visual scenes; Appendix D retains the same qualifications and interpretations.

D1.justification: Data-curation instructions, model initialization, hyperparameters, hardware, training-time measurements and code/data release statements are unchanged. Adding the word 'Appendix' to existing cross-references discloses no new implementation information.

R1.justification: v3 adds seven general vision-language references to the introduction and Rafailov et al. (2023) to the existing DPO discussion. These additions broaden background attribution without substantively changing research positioning or novelty claims.

P1.justification: v3 replaces the Preprint header with the ICLR 2026 publication header, adds funding acknowledgments before the references, clarifies appendix cross-references and makes limited wording, punctuation and capitalization corrections. The narrative and section organization remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: The same 20 figures and 17 tables are retained. Changes include limited caption and table emphasis, table sizing and spacing, and page reflow; the plots and illustrated scientific content are unchanged.

improvement.justification: v3 modestly improves documentation through explicit attribution of the existing DPO comparison, funding acknowledgments, clearer appendix references and small language corrections. The methods, empirical evidence, reproducibility details and limitations remain unchanged, so the overall benefit is limited to attribution, transparency and presentation.
